title: THE RIGHT HEART, THE WRONG HANDS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "One day, after Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were and watched them at their hard labour. He saw an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, one of his own people. Looking this way and that and seeing no one, he killed the Egyptian and hid him in the sand." - Exodus 2:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses had every advantage — palace education, royal status, comfort. And he walked out of it deliberately to look at his suffering people. Hebrews commends this choice: he chose mistreatment with God's people over the fleeting pleasures of sin (Heb 11:24-26). That part was right.

What follows was not. He looked this way and that — the classic movement of someone who knows he is doing wrong — and he killed a man, then buried the body.

Here is the tension. Moses had a genuine calling to deliver his people, and a genuine compassion for them. But he tried to accomplish God's purpose by his own strength, in his own timing, in a way God had not sanctioned. Right burden, wrong method.

We do this too. We see a real injustice and respond with rage. We see a real need and manipulate to meet it. A godly desire pursued in an ungodly way is still sin.

God did not discard Moses. But He did take him into the wilderness for forty years to teach him a different way.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where am I trying to accomplish something good by wrong means?
2. Do I look around to see who is watching before I act?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, purify not just my desires but my methods. Keep me from doing Your work in the flesh. Amen.
